headline: Paper reports cross-model transfer of interpretability tools when mapping prompts cover the tool's operating region
summary: In arXiv:2611.12675v1, submitted Nov 9, the authors report transferring three interpretability tools across 110 ordered pairs of 11 instruction-tuned open-weight models. A map fit on ordinary questions recovered 54% of the target's native refusal-steering effect on average; adding 16 harmful and 16 harmless prompts per target raised reported recovery to 102%, while control directions recovered at most 1%. The paper argues that transfer depends on whether map-training prompts cover the tool's operating region. Main experiments use five seeds, but the results have not been independently reproduced and cover only three tools and this selected open-weight model set.
